# Parser errors (PHEL100-199)

The parser turns the token stream into forms. A code in this range means a delimiter or a token sits where no form can be built from it.

| Code | Error |
|---|---|
| [PHEL100](#phel100-unterminated-list) | Unterminated list |
| [PHEL101](#phel101-unterminated-vector) | Unterminated vector |
| [PHEL102](#phel102-unterminated-map) | Unterminated map |
| [PHEL103](#phel103-unterminated-set) | Unterminated set |
| [PHEL110](#phel110-unexpected-token) | Unexpected token |
| [PHEL120](#phel120-parser-error) | Parser error |

## PHEL100: Unterminated list

Enum case: `ErrorCode::UNTERMINATED_LIST`

The parser reached the end of the file with a `(` still open. The reported line is where the list was opened, not where the file ran out.

```phel
(inc 1
```

**Fix:** Add the closing `)`, or run `phel balance` to locate the missing one.

## PHEL101: Unterminated vector

Enum case: `ErrorCode::UNTERMINATED_VECTOR`

The parser reached the end of the file with a `[` still open. A `)` where the `]` belongs reports the same code.

```phel
[1 2
```

**Fix:** Add the closing `]`.

## PHEL102: Unterminated map

Enum case: `ErrorCode::UNTERMINATED_MAP`

The parser reached the end of the file with a `{` still open.

```phel
{:a 1
```

**Fix:** Add the closing `}`.

## PHEL103: Unterminated set

Enum case: `ErrorCode::UNTERMINATED_TABLE`

The parser reached the end of the file with a `#{` set literal still open. The code is spelled `UNTERMINATED_TABLE` from when sets were written as tables.

```phel
#{1 2
```

**Fix:** Add the closing `}`.

## PHEL110: Unexpected token

Enum case: `ErrorCode::UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`

The parser found a closing delimiter with no open form to close, or a reader prefix such as `'` or `^` with no form after it.

```phel
(inc 1))
```

**Fix:** Delete the extra delimiter, or write the form the prefix is waiting for.

## PHEL120: Parser error

Enum case: `ErrorCode::PARSER_ERROR`

The fallback code for a parser error that carries no more specific one, such as a keyword alias the parser cannot resolve. Editor diagnostics report it under this code; the terminal prints the same message with no code in front.

```phel
::nope/foo
```

**Fix:** Read the message: it names the token the parser rejected.
